findings.title: [P1] Restore interval cancellation when polling stops
findings.body: When callers invoke the cleanup returned by `startPolling`, the interval now continues indefinitely because its handle is discarded. This causes work after disposal, retains captured state, accumulates intervals across repeated starts, and can prevent Node.js processes from exiting.

findings.title: [P1] Restore removal of the message listener
findings.body: After an attach/dispose cycle, subsequent messages still invoke the supposedly detached handler because the returned cleanup is now empty. Repeated attachment cycles therefore retain stale handlers and can duplicate message processing.

findings.title: [P2] Restore removal of the registered message handler
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function no longer detaches the handler. Any socket message emitted afterward invokes stale callbacks; repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate listeners and duplicate side effects.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Cancel the interval when polling is stopped
findings.body:
The interval handle is discarded and the returned cleanup is a no-op. After consumers stop polling, `refresh` continues every second indefinitely; in Node.js the active interval can also keep the process alive.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the cleanup returned by `attach` no longer unregisters the `"message"` handler. Messages emitted afterward still invoke stale handlers, causing duplicate processing and leaks across attach/dispose cycles.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore interval cancellation in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the cleanup returned by `startPolling` no longer stops its interval. `refresh` continues executing every second after disposal, potentially causing post-unmount work, repeated side effects, and preventing Node processes from exiting.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore interval cancellation in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
Every `startPolling` call creates an interval that can never be cleared. After callers invoke the advertised cleanup, polling continues indefinitely, retains `refresh` and its captured state, accumulates work across repeated starts, and in Node.js can keep the process alive.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore message-listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup no longer detaches the handler. Any reconnect, remount, or repeated attachment accumulates listeners, retains handler state, and causes every subsequent message to invoke stale handlers, potentially producing unbounded memory and processing growth.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
